title: Amazon: AI agents found and used a zero-day on their own
summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence reports that a threat actor it links with moderate confidence to China ran Cairn, an open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework, against East Asian universities for about 48 hours from 8 September 2026. Given only the goal of obtaining shell access, the agents spent about 16 hours on a hardened Redis target and ran credential sprays without success, then found a previously unknown path traversal flaw in the open-source MONAI Label medical imaging application and used it to get root on a server. Amazon notified the maintainers; the project's advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 (critical, 18 November) covers monailabel 0.8.5 and earlier, notes that authentication is off by default, and lists no patched release yet although the fix is merged. Gambit Security separately documented a financially motivated actor using Cairn against retailers.
why: The lesson for defenders is tempo: an agent that maps an API and finds a write primitive in minutes, then keeps trying for 16 hours, outpaces manual triage. Internet-facing research and AI apps (MONAI, Redis, Qdrant) are often deployed outside normal patching and auth standards.
todo: Do now: if you run MONAI Label (0.8.5 or earlier), take it off any reachable network, enable authentication (MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE is off by default) and track the advisory for a patched release; on 21 November it listed none.
Inventory internet-exposed AI and data services (Redis, vector databases, model servers) and require authentication on all of them.
Prefer high-confidence detections with automated containment for exposed services, as Amazon recommends; block the two IP addresses Amazon lists as indicators.
Amazon's post gives no CVE; the advisory says it was re-filed in the MONAI Label repository to obtain one (not verified here).
